% Files of the document that give a .4ht's name in \ProvidesFile, read
% with the primitive \input from the document's class beside it, and from
% the class's option file beside it. As in the PDF, each file's text is
% in the page, and tex4ht reads no .4ht of those names.
% - test-ownprim-class.cls reads test-ownprim/glossary.tex, named like
%   glossary.4ht.
% - test-ownprim-class10.clo, which the class reads with LaTeX's \input,
%   reads test-ownprim/index.tex, named like index.4ht. index.4ht defines
%   \printindex, which the PDF does not have, so the page shows that it
%   was read: a sentence the PDF does not have.
\documentclass{test-ownprim-class}
\begin{document}
Glossary: \ownprimglossary\par
Index: \ownprimindex
\ifdefined\printindex\par Index read for the web.\fi
\end{document}
